A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPFrame for crystal property prediction. All 18 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPFrame experiments on JARVIS and Materials Project, frame comparisons, efficiency measurements, and a PrBPt3 case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments integrating SPFrame with iComFormer and predicting JARVIS bulk and shear moduli.

M1.justification: The core frame construction and quaternion algorithm remain unchanged. Appendix A.9 adds an iComFormer adaptation that transforms interatomic edge vectors before computing lattice-relative angles for the edge-wise transformer, extending v1's eComFormer integration.

E1.justification: v2 adds bulk- and shear-modulus prediction on JARVIS in Table 5; v1 evaluated these properties only on Materials Project. Both datasets and all previously evaluated tasks remain.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged. The new JARVIS modulus comparison includes CrysGNN and CrysDiff, neither previously evaluated, and Table 4 adds the equivariant Gram-Schmidt local-frame comparator within the iComFormer experiment.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix A.5 and v2 Appendix A.8 state substantially different JARVIS configurations. Formation-energy width changes from 128 to 256 and learning rate from 0.001 to 0.0005; OPT bandgap changes from 800 polynomial-scheduled epochs to 500 cosine/warmup epochs; total-energy training changes from 500 to 1000 epochs and batch size from 64 to 32. Layer configurations also change, and new experiment protocols are added. These are reported setting revisions, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds a controlled examination of backbone generality, comparing unmodified iComFormer, its equivariant local-frame variant, and its SPFrame variant. The original frame ablations, efficiency analysis, and PrBPt3 visualization remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the PrBPt3 case-study values remain identical. Tables 4–5 substantially extend the results to another integrated backbone and JARVIS elasticity tasks. Newly reported iComFormer-SPFrame formation-energy MAE is 0.0250 eV/atom. For JARVIS bulk/shear moduli, SPFrame reports 9.357/8.963 versus Crystalframer's 8.876/8.999. These are additional experimental findings, not same-setting performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: New Appendices A.1–A.2 introduce a mutual-information superiority argument and an SE(3)-invariance derivation. v2 also corrects Equation 1 from an equivariance expression to invariance and fixes fractional-to-Cartesian conversion. The theoretical addition is substantial, although A.1 does not establish its claimed strict information advantage from feature-set cardinalities.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: combining invariant local frames with an equivariant global frame to preserve crystal symmetry and improve property prediction. The additional experiments and theoretical sections do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges weaker MP modulus performance and interprets the additional backbone experiments as evidence of generality. Appendix A.1 adds an interpretation in terms of retained target information. The limitations section narrows the missing theoretical analysis to a quantitative account of prediction accuracy.

D1.justification: The training appendix substantially revises existing recipes and expands from eComFormer-only documentation to separate backbone-specific settings. It supplies iComFormer widths, schedules, batch sizes, and SPFrame placement, plus configurations for JARVIS modulus tasks. Appendix A.9 also explains the new frame-to-angle integration procedure.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.6 substantially broadens research positioning beyond frame methods to pretraining, representation learning, and symmetry-aware crystal generation. It discusses methods including CrysXPP, CrysGNN, CrysDiff, SymmCD, Wyckoff Transformer, and WyckoffDiff, and explicitly distinguishes SPFrame's prediction objective from generative modeling.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include corrected figure references, expanded appendix organization and pointers, restructured training descriptions, acknowledgments, and affiliation/conference-header edits. This is a localized editorial revision rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–5, relocates the efficiency table, and removes the duplicate appendix quaternion algorithm while retaining Algorithm 1. The four existing figures and original result-table structures are preserved, with accompanying pagination and spacing changes.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone and elasticity experiments, expanded research context, and corrected invariance equation improve coverage and clarity. However, the new Appendix A.1 claims strictly greater target mutual information without establishing the required probabilistic mapping; unequal feature-set cardinalities cannot exclude equality. This introduces an unsupported theoretical guarantee alongside useful empirical additions, leaving no reliably assessable net direction in overall quality.
